items.title: Live: Israel deploys troops into southern Lebanon marking an escalation against Hezbollah
items.description: The United States and Israel are continuing to launch strikes at Iran as Tehran becomes increasingly isolated after attacking neighbouring countries. Follow live.

items.title: Australian family stuck in Doha say it is far too unsafe to fly
items.description: Marty and his family were on their way to Rome for a European vacation when they were evacuated off a Qatar Airways plane as missiles flew above.

items.title: Why the Middle East travel chaos could continue for much longer
items.description: Aussie travellers trapped in the Middle East recount missile strikes and late-night evacuations as thousands remain stranded with no end in sight.

items.title: The narrow strait of water putting oil prices and freight costs on the brink
items.description: Iran's threats to attack vessels in one of the most important shipping passages will strain global supply of oil and gas, experts say — and Australia will not be immune from the fallout.

items.title: Australian dollar, global stock markets dive as Middle East war intensifies
items.description: It follows a surge in the price of oil as Europe woke up to news the Strait of Hormuz had been closed to shipping.

items.title: Inside the election review the Liberal Party tried to keep hidden
items.description: Senior decision makers responsible for the Liberal Party's disastrous federal election defeat largely failed to critically assess their own performance in the aftermath, according to a controversial internal review.

items.title: Key moments from the Clintons' Epstein testimonies
items.description: More than nine hours of footage of Bill and Hillary Clinton's depositions on their alleged ties to Jeffrey Epstein have been released. Here are the key takeaways.

items.title: Restaurant fined $40k after children served citronella instead of cranberry juice
items.description: The former owner of a Perth restaurant is fined after a pair of sisters were served insect repellent instead of the juice they had ordered.

items.title: Kyle and Jackie O remained steadfast through scandals but the writing was on the wall
items.description: Jackie "O" Henderson has given notice saying she can no longer work with Kyle Sandilands, bringing an end to the Kyle and Jackie O Show.

items.title: Teen who threatened to 'assassinate' PM and Chris Minns says he did not mean it
items.description: A 19-year-old WA man admits threatening to kill the PM and NSW premier in a direct message to Chris Minns on Instagram.

items.title: Tina Arena was Unstoppable, until she wasn't
items.description: Music artists Tina Arena and Ngaiire have reimagined Sia's Unstoppable while opening up about how life-saving donated blood brought them back from the brink of serious illness.

items.title: Last blood moon for almost three years stuns stargazers
items.description: Australians looking to the sky on Tuesday night saw the Moon turn a reddish-orange hue, in the last total lunar eclipse until 2029.

items.title: Head rejects claim 'fully committed' Australia didn't care about T20 World Cup
items.description: Travis Head hits back at the public narrative that has followed Australia's surprise early exit from the T20 World Cup.

items.title: 'Our heart goes out to them': Matildas star lauds Iran players' bravery
items.description: The Matildas are expressing their sympathy while sharing a hotel with Iran's players ahead of this week's crucial Asian Cup clash.

items.title: A town in the Swiss Alps stood for 800 years. In an instant it was wiped out
items.description: The Swiss Alps are a natural wonder and a key part of the national identity, but life in the mountains is under threat from climate change.

items.title: Illegal foreign vessel, fishers seized by ABF in Cape York river, eyewitnesses say
items.description: An illegal foreign fishing vessel and nine men aboard have been intercepted by Australian Border Force off the far northern coast of Queensland, according to eyewitness reports.

items.title: Can you ask a neighbour to cut or trim a large tree?
items.description: Whether you're worried about how old mate's tree next door will hold up in the summer storms, or it's just creating more work for you on the weekend, knowing where you stand can be helpful.

items.title: Unauthorised direct debits create chaos for Perth business
items.description: A Perth business owner who has had $60,000 taken from his bank accounts via direct debits he did not approve says he has no option but to close accounts after his bank told him there was nothing more it could do.

items.title: Satellite images show destruction at huge oil refinery, Iranian nuclear facility
items.description: Newly released satellite imagery shows the aftermath of an Iranian drone attack targeting one of the world's largest oil refineries.

items.title: ABC Timelines quiz: Test your memory of the 2020s ... so far
items.description: We're back with the second part of our test of your memory of some of the major events of the 2020s in pop culture, sport and world news. Your challenge is to pick which happened first.

items.title: Former doctor 'banned indefinitely' over 'sexually motivated' examinations
items.description: A Queensland former doctor has been indefinitely disqualified from reapplying for registration after a tribunal found he excessively performed pap smears, breast checks and vaginal examinations on female patients.

items.title: Police wrongly granted bail to Kelly Wilkinson's murderer days before her death, inquest hears
items.description: Queensland Police wrongly granted bail to a man charged with the rape of his estranged wife nine days before he brutally murdered her in 2021, a coronial inquest has heard.

items.title: Video of teens catching critically endangered shark sparks probe
items.description: At least one grey nurse shark is dead and others have been injured by fishers on the NSW Central Coast.

items.title: Man acquitted of 2009 murder later confessed twice, court hears
items.description: The man is only the second person previously acquitted to be charged with murder under the state's double jeopardy laws, after he allegedly confessed to police twice.

items.title: Call to abolish prison strip searches as report find most find nothing
items.description: A report based on data from prisons across the country has found the majority of strip searches in prisons do not find contraband. The authors of the study are calling for an end to what they say is a traumatising and degrading practice.
